items.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013
items.q: my father ... was assisted by this great American named — what was his name — Varian Fry

ctx.x: And you yourself had a — I guess after going to Denmark there was an underground system?

Yeah. Well actually, this is April 9th is not? It is April 9th today? April 9th was the day that the Germans occupied Denmark. April 9, 1940. I remember it very well because it was the second time in my life that Nazis marched into a city that I was living in. When I was in Vienna I had scarlet fever at the time of the Anschluss. But I remember, that was considered a serious illness then, and that was one reason why my mother stayed with me and my father had to get out in a hurry. So he split and went to France.…

good place for a painter, for a studio, because there was plenty of light. And when I woke up I heard planes and I looked out and I could see the German — that cross that they had on their wings there, and then the swastika on the tail. So that was the Germans coming into Denmark, which was not a happy awakening. The planes dropped leaflets that the Germans had come to protect Denmark against the British and whatever. Anyway, it was interesting because the early part of the occupation, the Germans needed Denmark…
